section_summary: This section records the proceedings, interpellations, and legislative developments of the 73rd, 74th, and forthcoming 75th sessions of the Japanese Imperial Diet from early 1938 through late 1939 as reported by the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo and reviewed by the State Department. It details official statements and Diet interpellations of Foreign Minister Koki Hirota regarding the China Incident, third-power relations, unsuccessful German peace mediation, the decision not to formally declare war, cultural affairs, and regional developments in Inner Mongolia and Shandong. It further documents the passage of record-setting multi-billion yen wartime budgets and sweeping authoritarian economic legislation—most notably the National General Mobilization Law and the Electric Power Control Law—under the Konoe and Hiranuma Cabinets, marking the increasing subordination of parliamentary politics to military and state control.

subfiles.about: Translations of Diet proceedings containing Foreign Minister Koki Hirota's replies to interpellations on foreign relations, secret German mediation, and the China Incident.
subfiles.summary: Enclosures to Tokyo Despatch No. 2763 transmitting translations of Official Gazette Extra (Kampo Gogai) records from January 25–29, 1938, containing Foreign Minister Koki Hirota's responses to parliamentary interpellations. Hirota addresses diplomatic relations with Great Britain and other third powers, secret peace negotiations with China mediated by Germany, compensation and relief for Japanese interests in China, and the legal rationale for avoiding a formal declaration of war. He also details state-backed cultural programs, research on opium in China, the preservation of Chinese cultural relics, support for the autonomous government of Suiyuan-Chahar in Inner Mongolia, and claims regarding the Kiaochow-Tsinan Railway in Shantung.
subfiles.title: Enclosures to Despatch No. 2763: Translations of Diet Interpellations and Foreign Minister Hirota's Replies

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Despatch No. 2735 regarding the opening and New Year adjournment of the 73rd Diet session.
subfiles.summary: A Document File Note cross-referencing Despatch No. 2735 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, filed under 894.00 P.R./121 and dated January 18, 1938. The note records that the 73rd Session of the Diet was formally opened by the Emperor on December 26 with an Imperial Rescript, that the 1938-39 draft budget approved by the Cabinet was distributed to members of both Houses, and that the Diet adjourned on December 27 for the New Year recess until January 20.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Despatch No. 2735 Regarding Opening of the 73rd Session of the Diet

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting Foreign Minister Hirota's remarks to the Lower House budget committee concerning the Nine Power Treaty, China, and international organizations.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 186 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo reports press accounts of statements made by Foreign Minister Hirota before the Lower House budget committee on March 18, 1938. Hirota stated that the Nine Power Treaty had only nominal existence with abrogation to be expected in due course, denied Japanese territorial ambitions in China, and noted that formal recognition of the Provisional Government of China would be premature. He also stated that Japan's withdrawal from the International Labor Office would perhaps occur, while relations with the Permanent Court of International Justice would be maintained.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 186 Regarding Foreign Minister Hirota's Statements on the Nine Power Treaty and Foreign Policy

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Telegram No. 38 regarding Japan's China policy and Diet statements by Prince Konoe and Foreign Minister Hirota.
subfiles.summary: A Document File Note cross-referencing Telegram No. 38 from Tokyo, filed under 793.94/12314a and dated February 4, 1938. The telegram reports on developments in the Sino-Japanese conflict, specifically Japan's withdrawal of recognition from the Chinese National Government and the potential for a formal declaration of war, quoting statements delivered in the Diet by Foreign Minister Hirota and Prime Minister Prince Fumimaro Konoe.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Telegram No. 38 Regarding Sino-Japanese Conflict and Diet Statements

subfiles.about: An internal State Department memorandum calling attention to Tokyo Despatch No. 2850 reviewing the 73rd Japanese Diet.
subfiles.summary: An internal memorandum written by James K. Penfield of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, dated April 21, 1938, concerning Tokyo Despatch No. 2850 of March 31. The note highlights that the despatch reviews the accomplishments of the 73rd session of the Japanese Diet and lists 86 bills enacted, specifically advising the reader to examine the first two and a half pages.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 2850

subfiles.about: A comprehensive report by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew analyzing the legislation, political developments, and budgets of the 73rd Japanese Diet, with an enclosed press editorial.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 2850 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew details the closing of the 73rd Japanese Diet on March 26, 1938, underscoring the overwhelming parliamentary support for the government's sweeping legislative agenda and wartime mobilization. Grew reviews the passage of the National General Mobilization Law and the Electric Power Control Law, budgets totaling nearly eight billion yen, and lists all 86 enacted statutes. The despatch also describes the expulsion of Shakai Taishuto Diet member Suehiro Nishio for urging Premier Konoe to emulate Mussolini, Hitler, or Stalin, analyzes Konoe's strengthened standing, and encloses an editorial clipping from The Japan Times evaluating the session.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2850: Seventy-Third Japanese Diet

subfiles.about: A Department of State charge slip indicating the withdrawal of file document 894.032/189 from the archives.
subfiles.summary: A Department of State charge slip dated December 4, 1944, recording the charging out of document file 894.032/189 from the departmental archives. The form notes clerical tracking numbers and initials documenting the file's temporary removal.
subfiles.title: Department of State Charge Slip for File 894.032/189

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Telegram No. 44 regarding Diet interpellations on foreign policy, the budget, and the China conflict.
subfiles.summary: A Document File Note cross-referencing Telegram No. 44 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, filed under 894.00/839 and dated January 24, 1939. The note records that the telegram reported on interpellations in the House of Peers and the Lower House concerning foreign policy, the national budget, and the military conflict with China.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Telegram No. 44 Regarding Diet Interpellations

subfiles.about: An internal State Department memorandum summarizing Ambassador Grew's report on the achievements and significance of the 74th Japanese Diet.
subfiles.summary: An internal memorandum prepared by the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, dated May 3, 1939, summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 3808 regarding the 74th session of the Japanese Diet. It reviews the session's accomplishments, including passing budgets nearing ten billion yen and numerous regulatory statutes, and assesses its political significance, noting the parties' total acquiescence to the government, the temporary abatement of single-party movement pressures, and the uncertain future of Japanese parliamentary institutions.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 3808

subfiles.about: A detailed despatch by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reporting on the 74th Japanese Diet under Prime Minister Hiranuma, with an enclosed statement by the Premier.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 3808 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reviews the 74th session of the Japanese Diet ('Asia Promotion Diet'), which concluded on March 26, 1939, following the rise of the Cabinet of Prime Minister Baron Kiichiro Hiranuma. Characterized by unprecedented harmony and numerous secret sessions, the Diet passed record budgets of nearly ten billion yen and 89 bills—including state controls over rice distribution, religious organizations, shipbuilding, light metals, and aviation—with virtually no resistance. The despatch discusses the subdued nature of debates, the resignation of single-party advocate Seigo Nakano, the growing network of 'national policy' companies, and the compliant status of political parties under wartime mobilization, and encloses Prime Minister Hiranuma's official statement praising national unity.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3808: 74th Session of the Japanese Diet

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting the imperial ordinance setting the convocation date for the 75th session of the Imperial Diet.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 593 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo, dated November 11, 1939, reports that an Imperial ordinance promulgated on November 10 fixed December 23, 1939, as the official convocation date for the 75th session of the Imperial Diet.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 593 Regarding Convocation of the 75th Diet Session
